title: Transformer-XL: Attentive Language Models Beyond a Fixed-Length Context
authors: Z. Dai, Z. Yang, Y. Yang, J. Carbonell, Q. Le, R. Salakhutdinov
before: Transformers processed fixed segments with no memory between them.
problem: Context was capped by the segment, and text was chopped arbitrarily at segment boundaries.
breakthrough: Reuse hidden states from the previous segment and encode position relatively rather than absolutely.
why: The first serious attack on the context-length limit, and the origin of relative position encoding.
next: Sparse attention, then RoPE and ALiBi, then the long-context race.
inherits: Relative position encoding and the idea that context length is an engineering target.
